options.name: Spacing
options.reason: spacing takes any number of 4 px units; the stories draw 0 (the joined bar) and 2 (separate items, Onboarding). The gap of 2 binds the spacing scale's step 2, which is 2 x space.unit in every preset (SB-0121).

accessibility.accessibleNameSource: Host aria-label is forwarded to the group; a group of toggles needs a name when its purpose is not clear from the surrounding text. Each item is named by its text or its own aria-label.
aria: group: role="group" with the forwarded aria-label

items are native buttons with aria-pressed for both selections (APG toolbar and toggle button patterns). Single mode keeps aria-pressed rather than radio semantics because a pressed item can be pressed again to clear it, which a radio cannot do.
roving tab stop: one item has tabindex 0, the others -1; arrows move focus only, they do not press
disabled items are skipped by the arrows and are not focusable
accessibility.focusRingVisible: :focus-visible on the item; 3px solid ring in toggle-group.focus-ring.color; the focused item paints above its neighbours.

formAssociation.note: Not a form field. formAssociated only to follow <fieldset disabled>.

keyboard.Tab: enters the group on one item (the first pressed item, else the first enabled one) and leaves it

accessibility.missingNameWarning: Console warning, once per element (in every build), when the host has no aria-label. A name from an outer legend or label is not detected.

antiPatterns.pattern: Toggle Group as a required single choice in a form
antiPatterns.why: A pressed item can be pressed again to clear it, and nothing is submitted

antiPatterns.alternative: Set aria-label on every icon-only sb-toggle-group-item
antiPatterns.why: The buttons have no accessible name

antiPatterns.pattern: Group without a name when its purpose is unclear
antiPatterns.why: A screen-reader user hears bare buttons

useCases.when: Related on/off options such as text formatting
Pick one of a few views or alignments that can also be cleared

anatomy.name: group
anatomy.notes: div role=group in the shadow root; named by the host's aria-label.

default.notes: The items. Their order is the roving-focus order.

anatomy.name: button
anatomy.notes: Native <button aria-pressed> in the shadow root.

default.notes: Text, an icon, or both. An icon-only item needs aria-label.

click.note: Pointer, Enter or Space. Cancelled while disabled.

elements.notes: Must be a direct child of sb-toggle-group. The group sets data-position (first, middle, last, only) on slotchange; the item sets data-pressed from the group's value.

disabled.note: Disables this item only; it is skipped by the arrows.

value.note: Identifies the item in the group's value.

elements.summary: One toggle button of a sb-toggle-group. Takes variant, size and orientation from the group.

change.note: Fired after a person changes the pressed items. Not fired when value is set from code.

openQuestions.answer: aria-pressed buttons in role=group, both types.
openQuestions.question: Single mode: radio semantics (role=radio, aria-checked) or aria-pressed?
openQuestions.recommendation: aria-pressed on native buttons in both types: single mode lets the pressed item be cleared, which a radio cannot, and the APG toolbar pattern uses toggle buttons. A required one-of-many choice is Radio Group.

openQuestions.question: Roving focus in multiple mode too?
openQuestions.recommendation: Yes, both types: one tab stop and arrows, like the APG toolbar. Selection never follows focus.

openQuestions.question: Shape of value?
openQuestions.recommendation: string[] on the property for both types; space-separated on the attribute. One shape keeps type switching simple.

openQuestions.question: Per-item variant and size?
openQuestions.recommendation: No: the group sets them (items inherit from the group). Add later if needed.

selection.note: single: at most one item is pressed (pressing it again clears it). multiple: any number.

spacing.note: Gap between items in 4px units. 0 joins the items into one bar with shared borders.

value.note: Values of the pressed items. Property: string[]. Attribute: space-separated values.

contract.summary: Related on/off controls in one row: pick exactly one, or turn several on, like text alignment or formatting (Web Components).

# Plan: Toggle Group (planning gate)

Status: Approved under SB-0011 (owner pre-approval, 2026-11-08).

## Scope
`sb-toggle-group` and `sb-toggle-group-item`: a set of toggle buttons. `selection` single or multiple, `variant`, `size`, `spacing`, `orientation`, `value`, `disabled`, `change`. Roving focus through `src/controllers/roving-focus.ts`. State shared with `@lit/context`; the group writes `data-position` on slotchange.

## Files (in build order)
| Step | File |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | `src/components/toggle-group/ToggleGroup.stories.ts` |
| 2 | `playwright/tests/toggle-group/toggle-group.behavior.spec.ts` (written first, must fail) |
| 3 | `ToggleGroup.scss` -> `ToggleGroup.styles.ts` (generated; one sheet for both elements) |
| 4 | `ToggleGroup.ts`, `ToggleGroupItem.ts`, `context.ts`, `index.ts` |

## Test plan (test-first)
- Group is `role=group` named by aria-label; items are buttons with aria-pressed.
- single: pressing moves the selection, pressing again clears it; multiple: independent. `value` property and attribute; `change` composed, once, `detail.value`; no change for code updates.
- Roving: one tab stop (first pressed, else first enabled), arrows wrap, Home/End, vertical axis, RTL reverses, disabled skipped, arrows never press.
- Group disabled and item disabled; fieldset disabled.
- Layout: joined (spacing 0) shares borders and only outer corners round; spacing > 0 gaps; data-position values; vertical stacks.
- Token colors, focus ring keyboard-only, axe clean.

## Accessibility deviations from the references
- Solid 3px focus ring instead of ring/50.
- Single mode uses aria-pressed, not radio semantics (the visual reference uses radio there): the item can be cleared.

## Open questions (recommendation first)
- Q1 radio vs pressed: pressed. Answered.
- Q2 roving in multiple: yes. Answered.
- Q3 value shape: string[]. Answered.
- Q4 per-item variant/size: no. Answered.
